notes: Tier = APPARENT complexity from prompt text alone (the only signal available at routing time). Borderline examples are intentional: they define the boundary. See `boundary` field on contested seeds.

tierDefinitions.cheap: Mechanical, locally-scoped, unambiguous. No reasoning about system behavior. Renames, formatting, single-line edits, plain explanations of local code.
tierDefinitions.mid: Needs understanding across a file or a bug's symptoms, but the path is fairly clear. Symptom debugging with bounded scope, moderate refactors, writing tests.
tierDefinitions.frontier: Multi-file reasoning, subtle/emergent bugs, architectural decisions, anything expensive if wrong. Concurrency, design tradeoffs, hard-to-reproduce production issues.

examples.boundary: mid/frontier — reads mid, but CI-only failures (env, timing, ordering) can be frontier-hard. Labeled on apparent complexity.
